mentl/c3ba015:
The synthesized-family repr floor was sized for deletion against the
O(1) column read that landed at fe4b88b2. Probing the sizing before
spending it refuted two of its claims and found a live capability hole.

The floor is not a fabrication awaiting a better read: it is the word
face. A lambda or nested fn with an unused Gain param runs, because the
caller boxes the f64 into a cell and the callee signs i32 — both speak
the word face, and when the param is used the $wf$ twin appears and
derefs. Reading the declaration there would only add a twin.

At a handler arm it is the opposite. perform pushes emit_args_word --
every wide arg boxed, the arm's ABI declared floor-words in its own
comment -- then direct-calls the arm, whose signature is projected from
its param repr. Ignore the arg and the floored param matches the boxed
word; read it and the same call refuses: expected [i32, f64] but got
[i32, i32], zero diagnostics. So an arm cannot use a wide op argument,
and flooring is what hides it. The briefed deletion, executed as
written, would have given the ignored case its real width and broken it
too.

mn-arm-wide-op-arg.mn banks the pair. It is not wired into the frontier
gate: a red leg refuses every pin, and the fix is DEP-gated -- keying
the perform's call on the callee's word face needs arm params to carry
declared widths, which needs the emitfn note to carry params as it
carries captures. graph_emitfn_at's origin is param-bearing for two of
six kinds; EfkArm notes the body handle and lower holds zeros for arm
param handles. Both halves land together or each breaks the other's
case.

mentl/c36707f:
Pipe-forward semantics: Mentl fns are NOT auto-curried per
"Parameters ARE tuples" — `f(a, b)` calls f with the 2-tuple
(a, b), not as a curry chain. So `x |> f(a, b)` IS the full call
`f(x, a, b)` — left as the FIRST argument, then explicit args.

Pre-fix lowering of PForward produced curry-form
`LCall(LCall(f, [a, b]), [x])` — calling the result of f(a, b) as
if it were a closure. For non-curried f, this passes wrong arity:
emit produced `call_indirect (type $ftN)` where N = args.len of the
PARTIAL call, mismatching the real fn's signature. Empirically the
wheel's `nodes |> graph_extend_to(handle+1) |> list_set(handle,
GNode(...))` produced a chain of mis-arity call_indirect that
trapped at runtime.

Substrate move: $lower_pipe_forward inspects lo_r's tag — if
LCall (308) or LSuspend (325), unfold its (fn, args) pair and
prepend lo_l → flat LCall(fn, [lo_l, args[0], args[1], ...]). Bare
form (lo_r isn't a call) stays `LCall(lo_r, [lo_l])`. Wheel-side
mirror in src/lower.mn matches via destructuring on `LCall(_, fn,
args) => LCall(handle, fn, [lo_l] ++ args)`.

    post: (state, 5, 3, $add) → call_indirect $ft3 → x (one call,
          correct shape)

mentl/c307d7b:
Previous heuristic checked only the first byte — unreliable because the
low byte of a heap pointer can be in the printable ASCII range (32-126).
Now checks first 4 bytes: ALL must be printable ASCII to classify as
string. A heap pointer's bytes include 0x00 (null) for addresses < 64KB,
which correctly fails the check and dispatches to list_concat.

The val_concat heuristic remains fundamental debt — the correct solution
is full type inference for ++ dispatch. But 4-byte check is much more
reliable than 1-byte for the bootstrap path.

sonido/c3a1e91:
Root cause of LED-not-blinking in all audio examples: the SAI DMA buffers
(TX_BUFFER, RX_BUFFER) use #[link_section = ".sram1_bss"] and must land
in DMA-accessible D2 SRAM1 at 0x30000000. Our memory.x had the correct
MEMORY regions but no SECTIONS block, making .sram1_bss an orphan section
placed at an unpredictable address by the linker.

When start_interface() fired the first DMA transfer, it hit an invalid
address, triggering a bus fault → HardFault → Embassy executor halts.
No executor = no task scheduling = heartbeat never runs = LED never blinks.

blinky.rs worked because it never touches SAI/DMA.

Fix: add SECTIONS for .sram1_bss (→ RAM_D2_DMA, 0x30000000) and
.sdram_bss (→ SDRAM), matching the daisy-embassy reference memory.x.
The -R .sram1_bss objcopy flag correctly strips this NOLOAD section
from the flashed binary.
two-top/c399c00:
Implements the deterministic math layer per ARCHITECTURE.md:
- Fix (I16F16) and FixWide (I32F32) type aliases
- Vec2F with ZERO / new / from_cm / length_sq / length / normalize /
  dot / cross / rotate / angle / to_f32, plus Add and Sub impls
- sin / cos / sin_cos / atan2 / sqrt free functions wrapping cordic
- PI / TWO_PI / HALF_PI constants via Fix::lit

Property tests (proptest, all green):
- (a + b) - b == a for bounded Vec2F
- sqrt(x*x) ≈ x for non-negative bounded Fix
- sin² + cos² ≈ 1 across angles ±8 rad (exercises normalize_angle)
- rotate(v, TWO_PI) ≈ v
- normalize(v).length() ≈ 1 for non-zero v

Implementation notes:

- length() and sqrt() widen through FixWide before calling cordic.
  cordic's iterative sqrt squares candidates internally, which
  overflows Fix near Fix::MAX even when the mathematical result
  fits. Captured by a regression test (length_no_overflow_near_fix_max)
  and the proptest seed in tests/properties.proptest-regressions.
- length_sq returns Fix and saturates on overflow, matching
  ARCHITECTURE.md. Adequate for radius-scale comparisons; a wide
  variant can land later when arena-scale distance ranking needs it.
- to_f32 carries #[allow(clippy::disallowed_types)] — the only
  sanctioned float reference inside fixed_math.
- Trig/rotation test tolerances reflect Q16.16 precision (~5e-5
  absolute) scaled by component magnitude (±100 cm in proptests).
